questions.stem: What is the functional group in alcohols?
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the -OH (hydroxyl) functional group. This group determines the chemical properties of alcohols and distinguishes them from other organic families.

questions.stem: What is the general formula for alcohols?
questions.explanation: The general formula for alcohols is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH (or CₙH₂ₙ₊₂O). For example, methanol is CH₃OH (n=1) and ethanol is C₂H₅OH (n=2).

questions.stem: Which alcohol is commonly found in alcoholic drinks?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is the alcohol found in alcoholic drinks. It is produced by fermentation of sugars using yeast.

questions.stem: What are the products of the complete combustion of ethanol?
questions.explanation: Like other organic compounds, ethanol undergoes complete combustion in excess oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O.

questions.stem: Ethanol can be made by fermentation. What are the conditions needed?

options.text: High temperature (450°C), high pressure, and iron catalyst
Sugar solution, yeast (as a catalyst), warm temperature (30-40°C), and anaerobic conditions

questions.explanation: Fermentation requires sugar dissolved in water, yeast (which provides enzymes), a warm temperature (about 30-40°C), and anaerobic (absence of oxygen) conditions.

questions.stem: Why does ethanol dissolve in water, unlike most organic compounds?

options.text: Because it is a gas at room temperature
Because the -OH group can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules
Because it has a very low molecular mass

questions.explanation: The -OH group in ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, making short-chain alcohols miscible (fully soluble) with water.

questions.stem: Methanol is toxic and should never be consumed. What happens if methanol is ingested?

options.text: It is converted to toxic substances in the body that can cause blindness and death
It causes a mild headache only
It is immediately neutralised by stomach acid

questions.explanation: Methanol is very dangerous if ingested. The body metabolises it into formaldehyde and formic acid, which are highly toxic and can cause blindness, organ damage, and death.
